404.author: zy95-12
404.body:
Related: #339 (docs-only; keeps issue open — residual external picker). Related #352.

Folder import can work in a native browser while an external automation host rejects the same directory path. Add matching English and Chinese guidance to the existing Skills import guide so users can choose a complete-package alternative.

The note explains native Chromium `webkitdirectory` support, disabled Folder and ZIP/Git recovery in unsupported browsers (#352), and the remaining Scenario 2 Case A style host/driver limitation. It also identifies J11's successful directory `setInputFiles` coverage and explains that J11 is not blocked by that external picker gap. Only two Markdown files change.

Refs #339. Related: #352. This documentation follow-up leaves the external host limitation open.

## Validation

Candidate: `e54506e7`.

- `pnpm docs:check`: PASS, 141 Markdown files linted and checked for local links, 0 issues.
- `git diff --check`: PASS. Reviewed both translations against all five requested points and the existing J11 source.
- `pnpm ci:st`: PASS, 16 planned / 16 executed / 16 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: blocked at `NON_ROOT_REQUIRED` preflight, 4,311 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed / 0 assertion failures / 0 skipped; the runner verdict is FAIL because nothing ran. The same layer on unmodified upstream main (`8811fcad`) reproduced the same preflight and counts in a separate worktree.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: incomplete, 91 planned. The first research journey, AR-01 in `artifact-revision-mocked.spec.ts`, timed out at 180 seconds (0 passed, 1 observed failure). Stopped the remaining local run under memory pressure on this 3.4 GiB worker; no final aggregate counts were produced. A baseline E2E preparation attempt was also stopped before execution, so this timeout is not attributed as a proven upstream regression or a product regression.
- No product, UI, import pipeline, tests, or CI changes. No paid model tests were run.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable to the change: these are documentation-only edits with no changed product path. The attempted full local browser layer is reported separately above and did not reach J11; no new J11 pass is claimed. The documented J11 behavior is supported by its existing source and the passing current-head CI evidence recorded in #352.

## Release

Release category: release:docs

User impact: clearer Folder compatibility and complete-package ZIP/Git alternatives.

Compatibility and migration: none.

407.author: zy95-12
407.body:
The Agent can now request direct host execution when the user asks to skip the sandbox or the Agent judges it unsuitable, including while the selected Runner's sandbox is ready. Sandbox remains the default preference. This follows up the recovery work from parent #276.

Refs #406. Parent: #276.

- Make `operation_id` optional and accept `runner_id` for direct consent without a preceding failed sandbox call. Recovery IDs still pin the Runner and reject mismatched targets.
- Remove the sandbox-unavailable precondition in both API scope validation and Runner submission. Unreachable Runners fail with user/network-administrator guidance; no SSH repair is added.
- Preserve separate `direct_code` permission, exact command/target/account/workspace/Agent-run scope, one-use authorization and a new submission call after approval. Sandbox Always Allow and chat text cannot authorize host execution.
- Update prompt/tool guidance and execution documentation. Extend binding, Runner HTTP and production API journey coverage.

## Validation

Tested commit: `78a43a9e4af3681c23c5a1199874165f2107e724` (rebased onto upstream main).

- Focused UT: **163 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (`direct-execution.test.ts`, `workspace-bindings.test.ts`, workspace and prompt tests).
- Build: `pnpm build` passed. Test TypeScript: `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` passed.
- Documentation lint and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full local UT/ST preparation was interrupted by worker termination. Full UT/ST/mocked browser E2E are not claimed as passing; the requested resume prioritizes targeted validation. GitHub Actions will provide the full PR gates.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS: 20/20 numbered steps across 2 journeys; 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped.**

Production API/Runner CLI entry points, native Agent backend, a local scripted model and separately configured loopback remote Runner; no paid model calls or SSH.

- `node test/api/direct-execution-journey.mjs --ready`: ready-sandbox direct selection without a preceding sandbox attempt; local/remote denial, allow-once and allow-matching; execution audit/logs/workspace output; lost acknowledgements and unreachable target.
- `node test/api/direct-execution-journey.mjs`: sandbox-unavailable recovery plus the same permission, audit and transport-failure cases.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
User impact: direct execution can be explicitly authorized before sandbox failure. Compatibility and migration: none; existing recovery requests remain supported.
407.head: feat/406-agent-first-direct
407.title: feat(execution): allow direct consent before sandbox failure

408.author: sciencediscovery-bot[bot]
408.body:
Closes #309.

The artifact viewer was a small card — 1080×758 inside a 1920×1080 window — with a 560px preview inside it, so a report, a table or a plot was read through three nested scrollbars. It is now a large-screen content window whose content actually fills it.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css` | `.artifact-modal-panel` → `width: min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`, `height: min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`. `.artifact-modal-body` gets `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0` (it owns the leftover height and the scroll), header and mode tabs are pinned with `flex: 0 0 auto`. Markdown prose keeps a readable measure: `.markdown-body > :is(p, ul, ol, dl, blockquote) { max-width: 76ch }`. |
| `apps/web/src/styles/artifacts.css` | Inside `.artifact-modal-panel .artifact-modal-body` only: `max-height: none` for `.manuscript-preview`, `.artifact-source-preview`, `.dataset-table-wrapper`, `.notebook-cells`, and `.annotatable-figure img { max-height: min(760px, calc(100vh - 240px)) }`. Inline and timeline previews share those classes and keep their 560/460/420px caps. `.manuscript-preview pre` (fenced code blocks inside a report) deliberately keeps its 460px cap so a huge source file cannot stretch the panel into one endless column. |
| `apps/web/src/styles/memory-graph.css` | Stale comment on `.evidence-title` that still described the old fixed viewer size. |
| `apps/web/tests/ScientificArtifacts.test.tsx` | The #309 test now asserts the panel size, the 76ch measure, the body flex rule, the pinned header/tabs and the whole in-modal override block — plus counter-assertions that the base 560px / 460px caps survive. |

Review follow-up (HongyeZhou, `38a46e01`) is included: the taller window alone added blank space, so the rest of this PR is about making the content use it.

## Verification (specific to this change)

Measured on the **real `ArtifactModal` component** built from this branch with the repo's Vite config, served at a 1920×1063 viewport (the 1600×960 window), in headless Chromium:

| | Panel | `.artifact-modal-body` | Preview | Scrollbars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** (`f47ff584`), long markdown | 1600×960 | 614px tall, flex `0 1 auto`, ends 206px above the panel bottom | `.manuscript-preview` 560px, capped at 560px, scrolls inside itself | 2 (preview + body) |
| **Before** (`f47ff584`), source file | 1600×960 | 534px tall, ends 286px above the bottom | `.artifact-source-preview` 460px, self-scrolling | 2 |
| **After** (`38a46e01`), long markdown | 1600×960 | 818px tall, flex `1 1 auto`, bottom edge at 1011 vs panel bottom 1012 | 8865px tall, `max-height: none`, does not self-scroll | 1 (body) |
| **After** (`38a46e01`), source file | 1600×960 | 818px tall, same 1px gap | 15697px tall, `max-height: none` | 1 (body) |

Also measured after the change: `.annotatable-figure img` → `min(760px, calc(100vh - 240px))` = 753px at this viewport; fenced `pre` inside a report still 460px; and in a non-modal container the computed caps are still 560px (`.manuscript-preview`), 460px (source / table / notebook) and 420px (figure image), so inline and timeline previews are unchanged. Smaller windows behave as before: 1280×800 → panel 1200×633 with the same fill (body 491px, bottom 1px above the panel edge); `<=900px` still goes full screen.

### Screenshots (real component, 1600×960 window)

Long markdown report — top of the document:

![markdown preview, top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pr-assets-408/pr-assets-408/after-md-top.png)

The same report scrolled to the bottom: the document runs to the panel's bottom edge, no empty band:

![markdown preview, scrolled to the bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pr-assets-408/pr-assets-408/after-md-bottom.png)

Source file (`.py`, `kind: other`) — top:

![source preview, top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pr-assets-408/pr-assets-408/after-src-top.png)

For comparison, the same component at `f47ff584` (before the review follow-up): the 560px preview stops well above the window bottom:

![before the review follow-up](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pr-assets-408/pr-assets-408/before-md-top.png)

The screenshots live on the `pr-assets-408` branch so the PR diff stays CSS + tests only.

## Tests

- `apps/web`: `pnpm test` — 972/972 pass; `pnpm typecheck` — clean.
- CI: see the checks on `38a46e01` (L1 static checks, L2 mocked E2E slices, code check).

## Notes for the reviewer

- **What is not verified here:** the full app with a real backend, runner and artifact store — this environment cannot start the sandboxed E2E stack (no bubblewrap, no root). The screenshots and numbers above are the real component and the real stylesheets, but a human should still open one real long artifact, a wide table and a notebook at 1920 and confirm it looks right. Flagging this explicitly rather than calling the PR visually verified.
- `.manuscript-preview pre` keeps its 460px cap on purpose (see the table above). Say if you would rather have it lifted too.
- `DetailModal` and `EvidenceModal` share `.artifact-modal-body`, so they now scroll inside the fixed panel as well; previously their content could overflow past the panel's bottom edge.
408.head: fix/issue-309-artifact-viewer-size
408.title: fix(web): size the artifact viewer as a large-screen content window
